solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Others embracing US soldier, helping signing on process

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so the word for others wraps round the soldier

parts.note: the others are the rest
a GI is an American soldier
a helping or ration is a portion of food

explanation.surface: Someone describes how an American serviceman helps others through the process of enlisting.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrolling, or signing on for something, is the process of putting your name on an official list.

clue.text: Schemes king or queen employs

parts.note: R stands for rex (king) or regina (queen)
to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: A monarch makes use of plots and stratagems.
explanation.walkthrough: R serves for either Latin title, Rex or Regina, so 'king or queen' together yield one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tricks or stratagems meant to deceive are schemes, plural nouns both.

clue.text: Strangely mute, a gala in the country

indicators.note: done strangely, the letters of the words that follow are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: An oddly silent festival is held in some nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Named Central American nation, bordering Mexico, so an example of a country.

clue.text: Vivacity of Penny, on right lines boarding steam ship

indicators.note: passengers boarding a vessel go inside it, so these pieces go within the ship's letters

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it, so the penny comes first

explanation.surface: A lively penny travels along the correct route onto a steamer.
explanation.definitionFit: Liveliness and sprightly energy are the same quality as vivacity; both are nouns.

clue.text: Exposition concerning what may be drunk at dinner

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading

parts.words: what may be drunk at dinner
parts.note: port is a fortified wine often served after dinner

explanation.surface: A talk explaining the drinks served at a dinner party.
explanation.definitionFit: An account or written statement setting out facts is an exposition of them.

clue.text: A driver may go round in this

definitions.text: A driver may go round in this

parts.words: A driver may go round in this
parts.note: suggests a golfer's round or a motorist circling; literally the smallest circle in which a car can turn around

explanation.surface: Something a driver might circle within, like a golfer going round a course.
explanation.definitionFit: The term for the tightest circular path a vehicle can complete when steering on full lock.

clue.text: Ball that's gold and black

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Describing a ball coloured gold and black.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere or globe, such as the royal one in regalia, is a ball shape.

clue.text: Dull study beginning with articles in French and English

indicators.note: the study starts with the two articles placed ahead of it

parts.note: le is a French definite article
a is the English indefinite article
a den is a private room for study or work

explanation.surface: A boring study session that begins with French and English grammar on articles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' covers both French LE and English A, with 'and' joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy, sluggish and lifeless in the figurative sense, as leaden prose is dull.

clue.text: Good person goes by air for a bit of a flight

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good person

explanation.surface: A virtuous traveller chooses to fly, taking only a short part of the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests air travel, but it means a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A single step is one small part of a flight of steps in a building.

clue.text: Sailor in discussion failing to finish moral story

indicators.note: the sailor sits in the middle of the shortened discussion word
the last letter of the word for discussion is dropped

parts.note: a parley is a discussion, especially between opponents
AB is an able seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman tells an improving tale in a conversation that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sailor' is a crossword staple for the able seaman's abbreviation; 'failing to finish' drops the final letter of the discussion word, leaving PARLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A short tale teaching a lesson, like those in the Gospels, is a moral story.

clue.text: Observe ecclesiastical division

definitions.meaning: to observe is to notice with the eyes
a bishop's diocese, the area under a bishop

explanation.surface: Look at a church district.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means look at; the noun is a bishop's area of jurisdiction, as in the Holy See.

clue.text: His garden must be transformed and decorated

indicators.note: transforming the letters gives a new arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A man's garden has to be made over and prettified.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been adorned with a little parsley or lemon has been decorated.

clue.text: Girl is into history, an expert on Greece

indicators.note: the girl's name goes into the abbreviation for history

parts.note: Ellen is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman studying history becomes a specialist in Greek affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar of ancient Greek language and culture is a specialist on Greece.

clue.text: Celebrity needs time to get going

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A famous person needs a while before they can begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Beginning or setting off is getting going; both are infinitive verbs here.

clue.text: Nearest the leader for a short time

definitions.meaning: the runner-up, placed just behind first
a moment, as in 'wait a tick'

explanation.surface: Running just behind the front-runner for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming in after first place is runner-up position; separately, a very brief moment is one sixtieth of a minute.

clue.text: Medical pioneer's information, enthralling a learner

definitions.note: read as 'medical pioneer is', the apostrophe s being a link

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the information word holds the other letters

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
L is a learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A medical trailblazer's knowledge captivates a student.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek physician of the Roman era whose writings shaped medicine for centuries, an early pioneer of it.

clue.text: Sarah meeting boy, turning up in American city

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Sal is a short form of Sarah
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A girl meets a lad who arrives in a US city.
explanation.definitionFit: A large city in Texas, so an example of a city in America.

clue.text: Vicar with hair looking ridiculous in mock serenade

indicators.note: the letters, looking ridiculous, are jumbled into a silly new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman with a silly hairdo appears at a noisy mock serenade.
explanation.definitionFit: Raucous din of pans and kettles made outside newlyweds' house, a mocking serenade in folk custom.

clue.text: Temptress in short uniform

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: even means uniform, the same throughout

explanation.surface: A seductive woman wearing a skimpy uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first woman tempted Adam with the apple, so she is the archetypal temptress.

clue.text: In revolution you must capture soldiers who will want to kill you?

definitions.text: who will want to kill you?
definitions.note: a noun phrase: those who want you dead

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the letters are read backwards
the word for you captures, holding inside it, the soldiers

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
men means soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: During an uprising, you have to seize the troops before they murder you.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reuses the clue's second 'you'; the first is the archaic YE. 'In revolution' turns the combined YMENE round.
explanation.definitionFit: A foe or adversary is someone hostile who would wish you harm or death.

clue.text: Modern Kent town's economic policy

parts.note: new means modern
Deal is a seaside town in Kent, the English county; the apostrophe s links to the definition

explanation.surface: A recent policy for running the finances of a town in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: DEAL is a coastal town in Kent, a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Roosevelt's 1930s programme of reforms and public works in the US was an economic policy.

clue.text: One of the last characters to be heard in river

indicators.note: the letter is spoken rather than written, giving the sound of its name

parts.note: Y is one of the last letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A late letter of the alphabet is spoken aloud by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Wye flows along the England-Wales border.
explanation.definitionFit: Named watercourse in Wales and England, an example of a river.

clue.text: Country a bit on the cold side, we hear

indicators.note: the clue signals that a spoken word is meant, matching in sound

parts.words: a bit on the cold side
parts.note: chilly means rather cold

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a nation is somewhat cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Long narrow South American nation on the Pacific coast, an example of a country.

clue.text: Without giving up could give sister plenty

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged to give a new word

explanation.surface: Someone keeps generously giving to a sister without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something doggedly and continually, never stopping, is doing it without giving up.
